learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to classify production planning challenges in different industries and company sizes, as well as with regard to the distinction between long-, medium-, and short-term planning tasks.
Students are able to understand planning and control philosophies, especially according to Push and Pull principles, and their significance for production processes.
Students are able to practically develop simple production planning and control concepts and to select suitable production control procedures as needed.
Students are able to apply control and key figures for the evaluation and design of production planning tasks.
Students are able to assess digital production planning, particularly the role of PPS systems in the context of digitization and Industry 4.0.
Students are able to consider sustainability goals in production planning and logistics with a focus on the UN Sustainable Development Goals, especially SDG 9 and SDG 12.

For dual students: Dual students have reflected on experiences from their partner companies in light of the learned procedures and methods for production planning and logistics, and can demonstrate their application in concrete practical examples.
For dual students: Furthermore, they are able to analyze and evaluate the implemented procedure for production planning at their partner company.

syllabus_topics: PPS systems according to MRP II
Integration of PPS systems in ERP/CIM,... and Industry 4.0, digitization of production planning
Inventory models with corresponding key figures
Time management – scheduling and capacity planning
assessment_rules: The final grade is based on an oral examination of 15 minutes. For dual students, the oral examination will specifically address the transfer between theory and practice based on elements from their partner company.
